_note: Photos and drawings shown on the site. To add one: put the image in src/assets/photos/ (JPEG or PNG, long edge about 2400 px, metadata stripped) and add an entry here. experiments lists experiment slugs, or is empty for project-wide images; kind is photo or drawing (drawings are shown whole, not cropped). Videos live in public/media/video/. Credits and captions marked TBC need checking by the team.

photos.alt: Diagram of BABY 100 mL: helium flows from a cylinder over a 100 mL crucible of ClLiF salt set between two neutron sources, then on to tritium collection and a liquid scintillation counter.
photos.caption: How BABY works: (1) DT generators produce 14 MeV neutrons; (2) neutrons breed tritium from lithium in the salt; (3) the tritium moves through the salt; (4) it is released into the helium sweep gas or permeates the walls; (5) it is collected and counted by liquid scintillation. Used in the BABY guide.
photos.credit: Delaporte-Mathurin et al., Nucl. Fusion 65 026037 (2025), CC BY 4.0

photos.alt: A rack of white-capped sample vials labelled BABY 3.

photos.alt: A beige tritium bubbler unit with a temperature display and six small vials on its front panel.
photos.caption: A tritium water bubbler: the sweep gas bubbles through the vials, which capture the tritium; a furnace between the two sets converts insoluble forms so both are caught.

photos.alt: A gamma detector inside an open, copper-lined cylindrical shield on a lab bench.

photos.caption: Diamond detector electronics, used to monitor the DT neutron source during runs.
